key_insight: Small-radius, high-electronegativity A-site dopants such as Ca can simultaneously improve proton transport and chemical stability in BaCeO3-based perovskite electrolytes by weakening A–O bonding and modifying lattice/basicity effects.
engineering_relevance: A-site doping provides a practical materials-design route to make proton-conducting solid oxide fuel cell electrolytes more conductive, more CO2/SO2-resistant, and less prone to impurity phases.
method: Mechanistic analysis linking A-site electronegativity/radius to vacancy formation, proton uptake, and gas adsorption
Assessment of lattice contraction and Ca surface segregation effects
evidence_signal: The abstract reports computational evidence showing improved oxygen-vacancy formation, enhanced proton uptake, reduced acidic-gas adsorption, and better thermal stability for Ca-doped BaCeO3.
watch_item: Benefits may depend on composition and operating regime, and Ca segregation/grain-boundary effects will need careful control in real electrolytes.
paper_title: Role of small-radius and high-electronegativity A-Site dopants in enhancing proton transport and stability of perovskite electrolytes
